q.t: The opposite sides of a parallelogram are:
q.e: A diagonal splits it into two congruent triangles (ASA), so the opposite sides match.

q.t: The opposite angles of a parallelogram are:
q.e: They are matching angles of the two congruent triangles made by a diagonal.

q.t: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram add up to:
q.e: They are co-interior angles between a pair of parallel sides.

q.t: The diagonals of a parallelogram:
q.e: The four small triangles formed pair up as congruent ones, so each diagonal is cut in half by the other.

q.t: The diagonals of a rectangle are:
q.e: Each diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with the same two sides.

q.t: The diagonals of a rhombus meet at:
q.e: All four sides are equal, so each diagonal is the perpendicular bisector of the other.

q.t: Which shape has diagonals that are equal AND perpendicular bisectors of each other?
q.e: A square is both a rectangle (equal diagonals) and a rhombus (perpendicular diagonals).

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 70°. Find ∠C (in degrees).
q.e: ∠C is opposite ∠A, and opposite angles are equal.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 70°. Find ∠B (in degrees).
q.e: ∠B is adjacent to ∠A: 180 − 70 = 110.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, AB = 8 cm. Find CD (in cm).
q.e: CD is opposite AB, and opposite sides are equal.

q.t: Two adjacent angles of a parallelogram are in the ratio 2 : 3. Find the larger (in degrees).
q.e: They add to 180°: 5 parts of 36°, so 72° and 108°.

q.t: A parallelogram has perimeter 40 cm and one side 12 cm. Find the adjacent side (in cm).
q.e: Two adjacent sides make half the perimeter: 20 − 12 = 8.

q.t: The diagonals of a rectangle are 10 cm long and meet at O. Find the distance from O to any vertex (in cm).
q.e: The diagonals are equal and bisect each other, so O is 5 cm from every corner.

q.t: The diagonals of a rhombus are 6 cm and 8 cm. Find its side (in cm).
q.e: Half-diagonals 3 and 4 meet at right angles: 3² + 4² = 25, so the side is 5.

q.t: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are (3x − 10)° and (2x + 15)°. Find each of these angles (in degrees).
q.e: Opposite angles are equal: 3x − 10 = 2x + 15, x = 25, angle = 65°.

q.t: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram are (x + 30)° and 2x°. Find the larger angle (in degrees).
q.e: 3x + 30 = 180, so x = 50. The angles are 80° and 100°.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD the diagonals meet at O and AC = 14 cm. Find AO (in cm).
q.e: The diagonals bisect each other.

q.t: A rectangle has sides 5 cm and 12 cm. Find the length of its diagonal (in cm).
A rhombus has perimeter 52 cm. Find its side (in cm).
q.e: All four sides are equal.

q.t: A parallelogram with one right angle must be a:
q.e: The opposite angle is also 90°, and the adjacent ones are 180 − 90 = 90°. All four are right angles.

q.t: The diagonals of a rhombus are 24 cm and 10 cm. Find its perimeter (in cm).
q.e: Half-diagonals 12 and 5 give side 13. Perimeter = 4 × 13 = 52.

q.t: One angle of a parallelogram is 4 times its adjacent angle. Find the smaller angle (in degrees).
In parallelogram ABCD, the bisectors of ∠A and ∠B meet at P. Find ∠APB (in degrees).
q.e: ∠A + ∠B = 180°, so their halves add to 90°, leaving 90° for the third angle of △APB.

q.t: The diagonals of a rectangle are 10 cm long and cross at 60°. Find the length of the shorter side (in cm).
q.e: The triangle with the 60° angle has two sides of 5 cm (half-diagonals), so it is equilateral. The shorter side is 5 cm.

q.t: A rhombus has side 8 cm and one angle 60°. Find its shorter diagonal (in cm).
q.e: The shorter diagonal with two sides forms a triangle with two equal sides and a 60° angle between them — equilateral, so the diagonal is 8 cm.

q.t: A parallelogram has perimeter 60 cm and sides in the ratio 2 : 3. Find the longer side (in cm).
q.e: Two adjacent sides total 30 cm: 12 cm and 18 cm.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠DAB = 75° and ∠DBC = 60°. Find ∠CDB (in degrees).
q.e: AD ∥ BC, so ∠ADB = ∠DBC = 60° (alternate). In △ABD: ∠ABD = 180 − 75 − 60 = 45°. AB ∥ DC gives ∠CDB = ∠ABD = 45°.

q.t: A rhombus has side 10 cm and one diagonal 12 cm. Find the other diagonal (in cm).
q.e: Half of the known diagonal is 6. 10² − 6² = 64, so the other half-diagonal is 8 and the diagonal is 16.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, AB = (3x − 1) cm and CD = (2x + 4) cm. Find AB (in cm).
q.e: Opposite sides are equal: 3x − 1 = 2x + 4, x = 5, AB = 14.

q.t: The diagonals of parallelogram ABCD meet at O. AO = (x + 3) cm and OC = (2x − 5) cm. Find AC (in cm).
In rhombus ABCD, ∠ABC = 56°. Find ∠ACD (in degrees).
q.e: ∠BCD = 180 − 56 = 124°, and the diagonal AC bisects it: 62°.

q.t: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at O and ∠AOB = 110°. Find ∠OAD (in degrees).
In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = (2x + 25)° and ∠B = (3x − 5)°. Find ∠D (in degrees).
q.e: 5x + 20 = 180, so x = 32. ∠B = 91°, and ∠D is opposite ∠B.

q.t: ABCD is a square and CDE is an equilateral triangle drawn outside it. Find ∠AED (in degrees).
q.e: ∠ADE = 90 + 60 = 150°, and DA = DE (both equal the side). The isosceles △ADE has base angles (180 − 150) ÷ 2 = 15°.

q.t: The diagonals of a rhombus are in the ratio 3 : 4 and its perimeter is 40 cm. Find the longer diagonal (in cm).
q.e: Side = 10. Half-diagonals 1.5k and 2k: 2.25k² + 4k² = 100, so k = 4. Diagonals 12 cm and 16 cm.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, the bisector of ∠A meets DC at its midpoint E. AD = 6 cm. Find AB (in cm).
q.e: ∠DEA = ∠EAB (alternate) = ∠DAE, so △ADE is isosceles with DE = AD = 6. E is the midpoint, so DC = 12 = AB.

q.t: A rectangle has perimeter 46 cm and diagonal 17 cm. Find its longer side (in cm).
q.k: max(a for a in range(1,23) if a*a+(23-a)**2==289)
q.e: The sides add to 23 and satisfy a² + b² = 289. The pair 8 and 15 works (64 + 225 = 289).

q.t: One diagonal of a rhombus is equal to its side. Find the larger angle of the rhombus (in degrees).
q.e: That diagonal and two sides form an equilateral triangle, so one angle is 60° and the adjacent one is 120°.

q.t: A parallelogram whose diagonals are equal AND perpendicular is a:
q.e: Equal diagonals make it a rectangle; perpendicular diagonals make it a rhombus. Both together: a square.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A − ∠B = 40°. Find ∠C (in degrees).
